correctness.rationale: For arbitrary primes p<q and a positive periodic trajectory n_i, define c_i=qνp(n_i)+pνq(n_i)>0. Exact ratios n_{i+1}/n_i=c_i/(pq) imply product c_i=(pq)^L and every c_i has only p,q prime factors. Valuation updates give c_{i+1}−c_i=q(u_i−1)+p(v_i−1) if c_i=p^{u_i}q^{v_i}. Below pq, smoothness forces c_i to be p^u or q; c=p or q exits positivity, otherwise p^u increases. At/above pq, the half-line is forward invariant, including pure q^v via c_next>=q²−q+p>=pq. Thus no finite positive cycle can contain c<pq; all c_i=pq by product, hence every point is fixed. Integer congruence q a+p b=pq has only exponent solutions (p,0) or (0,q). Independently sampled 35,955 bounded trajectories over prime pairs through 29 with zero nontrivial cycles; this is supplementary to the unrestricted valuation proof.

originality.rationale: Talukdar and Saikia (2026) Theorem 3.4 already classifies positive fixed points for general supports; those families are explicitly not new. Their discussion names additional periodic points as further work. Published 2026 Resultary theorem excludes nontrivial cycles for {2,3}, but a single prime pair does not imply arbitrary p<q. The new universally quantified two-prime cycle exclusion, using a smooth threshold and orbit-product argument, survives these comparisons. General support size three remains unknown here.
residual_risks: An unindexed theorem treating all two-prime supports could exist despite absent in queried primary and published databases.
The classification does not extend to prime supports of size 3 or above or assert behavior of nonperiodic orbits.

value.rationale: Nontrivial periodic points in prime-supported arithmetic differential dynamics are a natural open structural problem highlighted by primary literature. Closing it uniformly for the entire family of two-element prime supports is a substantive classification and not just restating the known fixed-point formula or changing numeric parameters in the {2,3} theorem.

limitations: An unindexed theorem treating all two-prime supports could exist despite absent in queried primary and published databases.
